title: Q4 electronic-fence layout and capacity with nonzero initial inventory

initial_levels.meas343: 2017-05-16 00:00 snapshot: for every bike whose last trip started before the instant, the destination cell of that trip; trip durations are not in the data, so a trip starting before 00:00 is treated as completed by the snapshot. Bikes seen before the snapshot are assumed still in service. Shares are scaled to 343,638, the measured fleet total used since T006.
initial_levels.fleet495: Q1 minimum feasible periodic inventory occ0_j = max(0, -min_t cum_j(t)) with cum from full-scale Q1 arrivals (arr_q1_cell/0.128) minus full-scale observed departures (dep_obs/0.128), then normalised to 495,540. The raw sum before normalisation is 478,104.70, so only the shape is used, not the raw total.

settings.capacity_rule: Monte Carlo 95th percentile of the peak 15-minute occupancy; the trajectory starts at the fence's standing inventory and the peak includes t=0. Per-fence percentiles are not additive in probability, so their sum is a conservative deterministic sizing convention, not a city-wide simultaneous 95% guarantee.
settings.departures: Both demand surfaces use the same full-scale observed departures dep_obs/0.128; the Q1 surface changes arrivals only.
settings.frontier_cost: capacity slots + lambda * fences, lambda=150 slot-equivalents (knees also for 0 and 300).
settings.lambda_note: lambda=150 is a planning exchange rate (one fence is treated as worth 150 slot-equivalents), not an estimated construction cost; lambda=0 and 300 bracket the selection.
settings.selected_rule: primary plan = knee at lambda=150 on the meas343 capacity-coverage curve of each demand surface; 626 is reported only as a point on the frontier.
settings.night_note: T007 measured 21:00-06:00 at 39.34% of moved bikes; zero-initial / overnight-empty is not used.

magnitude_check.basis: full_coverage (all 5,263 cells inside some fence); the selected knee plan covers only ~77% of arrivals, so its capacity is not comparable with these fleet-wide ranges.
magnitude_check.selected_capacity_note: At the knee the selected plan's capacity is lower because the uncovered cells and their standing bikes lie outside the fences.

obs_fleet_excess.no_double_count_audit: standing_total equals 495,540 exactly (each bike counted once); the full-coverage plan assigns every cell to one fence, so buffer_total does not count any cell twice. The excess is therefore not double counting; the observed surface has sharper peaks than the Q1 surface.

q1_minus_obs.note: Raw capacity totals are confounded by the different coverage of the two knee plans (Q1 76.86%, observed 78.43%); the per-covered-arrival row is the comparable size difference.

validation.note: Hold-out comparison uses the two T005 test days (2017-05-12/19), excluded from the Q1 training set. The inventory comparison is the measured 5/16 00:00 drop-off snapshot against the minimum-feasible Q1 shape.

selected.definition: multiplicity counts how many selected fence sites lie within R of each cell; duplicate capacity = sum over cells of (I0 + max hourly arrivals) * (multiplicity-1), i.e. the slot count that would be counted twice if catchments were treated as overlapping.

code_changes.what: Q4 siting/sizing: two demand surfaces, two initial levels, exclusive greedy partition, Monte-Carlo 95th peak occupancy including standing inventory, cost-coverage frontier and knee selection.
code_changes.why: replace the zero-initial 0.2% self-check and the old frac_stop capacity count with reproducible evidence.

notes: Demand surfaces are full scale: arr_q1_cell and arr_obs_cell multiplied by 1/0.128; both sum to 2,143,417.41 arrivals/day. The earlier 4x bug (repeating an hourly total into four slots without dividing) is not present; to15 divides by 4 first.

meas343 is the 2017-05-16 00:00 snapshot: the destination cell of each bike's last trip starting before the instant, rescaled to 343,638. Trip durations are unavailable, so a trip starting before 00:00 is treated as completed.

fleet495 is the Q1 minimum-feasible periodic inventory occ0_j=max(0,-min_t cum_j(t)) from full-scale Q1 arrivals minus full-scale observed departures, normalised to 495,540; the raw sum is 478,104.70, so only its shape is used.

Capacity is the per-fence 95th percentile of the 15-minute occupancy peak, with standing inventory added at the start of the trajectory and included in the peak; it is never max-then-add. Summed per-fence percentiles are a conservative sizing convention, not a simultaneous city-wide 95% guarantee.

Attribution is exclusive: each picked fence claims only still-unassigned cells within 450 m, so every cell belongs to at most one fence. Geometric overlap is reported separately: Q1 selected 2,020 cells covered by 1 fence / 44 by 2 / 0 by 3+, multiplicity 1.0213, duplicate capacity 12,280 slots (2.80%); observed 1,965 / 45 / 0, multiplicity 1.0224, 3.09%. The old 1,799 / 37 / 0 and multiplicity 1.03 were a smaller overlapping layout; the 13%/22% figures on the full greedy path are not the selected plan.

The selected plan uses the lambda=150 knee (Q1 705 fences, 76.86% of arrivals; observed 687, 78.43%); 626 is retained only as frontier position (Q1 72.67%, observed 75.51%). The capacity bridge in q4_frontier.json separates standing inventory from buffer at 626, at the knee, and at full coverage; the old zero-initial 344,463 buffer was computed on overlapping catchments, so it is larger than the 237,653 exclusive buffer at 626.

Full-coverage capacity is 734,345 (Q1, meas343) and 747,816 (observed, meas343), inside the 600-750k check; fleet-level capacity is 884,585 (Q1) and 905,308 (observed, 0.59% above the 900k upper bound). The observed excess is not double counting: standing totals are exactly 495,540 and each cell is assigned once; the observed surface simply has sharper peaks.

R=450 m is a planning threshold, not a 2017 measured walking distance; 2026 OSM is only an external geographic check.
